title: Kingdom of Egypt
capsule: The Kingdom of Egypt was established on 15 March 1922 when Britain issued a unilateral declaration ending its protectorate, recognising the Sultanate of Egypt as an independent constitutional monarchy under Fuad I of the Muhammad Ali dynasty. British forces remained on Egyptian soil under a 1936 Anglo-Egyptian Treaty, and Britain retained control of Sudan and the Suez Canal Zone, making the independence partial; Fuad I and his son Farouk I clashed repeatedly with the Wafd Party over the constitution. The monarchy's association with continued British presence and military humiliation in the 1948 Arab-Israeli War fatally undermined Farouk's legitimacy, and on 23 July 1952 the Free Officers Movement led by Muhammad Naguib and Gamal Abdel Nasser overthrew the king; Farouk abdicated on 26 July 1952, and Egypt was proclaimed a republic on 18 June 1953.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Egypt's territorial extent during the monarchy period is well documented; the status of Sudan as Anglo-Egyptian Condominium rather than fully Egyptian territory introduces ambiguity in how broadly to draw the state's boundaries.
